messages:
maria_support: Escalation incoming — Novus Payments reported repeated JSON parse failures when using our structured output mode in prod (workspace: novus-payments, env: prod). They see 'Unexpected token' in their parser. Marking P1. Repro steps and examples below.

kevin_oncall: Oncall here. Thanks Maria — can you paste request_id + raw model response? Also grab the last 10 lines of the inference log. If this is a model-side regression we may need to rollback model variant.

maria_support: Request IDs: r-20260317-9a1b2c (first failure), r-20260317-9a1b9d (repeat). Raw response (received by customer):

```
{
  "transaction_id": "tx_7b3f",
  "status": "approved",
  "amount": 1250,
  "currency": "USD",
  "fraud_score": 0.02,
  "notes": "Processed by plugin X",
}
```

Their JSON.parse throws at the trailing comma after "notes". They also sometimes get: 

```
{"transaction_id":"tx_7b3f","status":"N/A","amount":null}
```

which breaks their strict schema (expects status in [approved,declined] and nulls only for optional numeric fields). They called with our SDK param: `structured: true, schema: payment_v2, strict_validation: true`.

kevin_oncall: That trailing comma indicates the model printed a list/object with human punctuation. Likely a generation artifact. Two immediate mitigations: 1) flip the workspace to `strict_validation: false` or `permissive_parse: true` so customer's parser tolerates comments/commas, 2) route Novus traffic to stable model variant v3.1.x. I'll start a model rollback canary.

sanjay_ml: Added: root cause hypothesis — v3.2.1 few-shot prompt examples include trailing commas in the reference outputs, which can prime the model to emit commas. Also we see "N/A" being used for unknowns (string) instead of null. Quick fixes: sanitize model string before returning to customer (post-processing step) to remove trailing commas and coerce common tokens (N/A, none, unknown) -> null when the schema expects null. I'll prepare a hotpatch to the response formatter. Estimated hotspot deploy: ~45–60 minutes if approved.

jess_account: We need a short customer comms template. Suggested message: "Hi Novus — we identified a generation/formatting regression that can produce non-strict JSON (trailing commas / string placeholders). Temporary workaround: set `strict_validation=false` in your SDK call or use our permissive parse feature. We're rolling a hotfix to sanitize output and may roll back to the prior model variant. We'll update within 1hr. Apologies for the disruption." Can someone from eng confirm SLA impact for their SLAs?

maria_support: Confirmed with Novus they hit this in checkout flows (high severity). I've already applied client-side mitigation on their tenant: set `strict_validation=false` and enabled `fallback_to_text=true` in case parsing fails. They reported immediate reduction in errors (from ~3% of txn to ~0.1%). I've also opened a support ticket NOVUS-3245 and posted the workaround steps in the customer portal.

deploy-bot: Rollout action: model-v3.2.1 -> rollback -> model-v3.1.9 started for novus-payments workspace (canary 10% -> monitor).

kevin_oncall: Monitoring logs now. Maria, please capture the failed raw responses (I've already pulled three samples) and add to the incident thread. Sanjay, please prioritize the post-process sanitizer as backup in case rollback is not enough. If sanitizer is trivial (regex to remove trailing commas & standardize N/A->null) we can deploy as infra hotfix.

sanjay_ml: I'll open a PR with sanitizer + unit tests for edge cases (arrays, nested objects). Quick regex may cover most cases but I'll be conservative — will run fuzzer against example outputs. PR link: (internal) will be posted in the thread in 20m. ETA for hotfix merge -> 45m, deploy -> 60m.

jess_account: I'll prepare the external comms and update the account timeline. Suggested SLA message: we expect full mitigation (rollback or hotfix) within 1 hour; we'll follow up with RCA within 48 hours.

maria_support: Customer notified with the suggested message, they acknowledged. Keeping this thread open until rollback/hotfix confirmed. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
